- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 1–2% for early periods.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 85+), overshooting by 2–5% in next 3–5 days; apply dampening factor to peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >85, reduce by 1–3% for next 5 days; if <80, increase by 0.5–1.5%.
- When sentiment is low and history shows volatility, model tends to smooth out extremes; add 0.5–1.5% noise to forecast to reflect market uncertainty.
- If forecast is >85 and true outcome is <82, model is overconfident; reduce by 2–4% for next 7 days unless sentiment is strong.
- If forecast is <80 and true outcome is >82, model is underconfident; increase by 1–3% for next 5 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
